parts.note: the doodlebug was the wartime nickname of the German V1 flying bomb, written V-one with a Roman numeral
devoured means ate

explanation.surface: An insect larva gobbled up a fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doodlebug' looks like an insect, but it is the Second World War V1 flying bomb, written VI.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot or travel in an aircraft is to fly, a verb sense shared exactly.

parts.note: an attaché is a junior diplomat; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: An embassy official's daughter has wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attached is spoken for, in a relationship or wed, an informal sense.

clue.text: Police officer crept in so cunningly

indicators.note: cunningly suggests the letters of crept in so are craftily rearranged

explanation.surface: A detective sneaked in with great cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank in the British police above sergeant, also a general title for detectives.

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of at rest are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor cares for a patient lying at rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' reads as a noun but is a verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who looks after a patient treats them; both are verbs for medical care.

indicators.note: the casual shoes are worn by the Tory, so the footwear goes around him

parts.note: sandals are casual open shoes
C stands for Conservative, the Tory party

explanation.surface: Political outrage over a Tory MP turning up in flip-flops.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural nouns: affairs that provoke public outrage are scandals, a close synonym.

parts.note: Com is a standard abbreviation for commander
somewhat means partly, in part
mental is informal for mad

explanation.surface: A commanding officer, a bit unhinged, is committed under mental health law.
explanation.walkthrough: To be sectioned in Britain is to be detained under the Mental Health Act; here it means divided.
explanation.definitionFit: Divided into separate sections or compartments, an adjective sense of the past participle.

parts.note: Norma is the druid priestess of Bellini's opera
N and S, North and South, are partners at bridge

explanation.surface: An opera heroine pairs up with invading Frenchmen.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1066 invaders of England came from Normandy in northern France.

indicators.note: the accomplished word goes round the single letter

parts.note: able means skilled, accomplished
read as maiden's head, the first letter of maiden; Maidenhead is an English town on the Thames

explanation.surface: A capable stroll round a Thames-side town.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidenhead, a Berkshire town, splits as head of maiden, giving M.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to stroll at a leisurely pace, a kind of walk.

clue.text: Make a mistake in retiring for a drink

indicators.note: the mistake verb goes inside the word for retiring

parts.note: retiring means shy, bashful
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A shy person slips up over a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified Spanish wine, a classic aperitif.

definitions.meaning: a fondness or preference, as in a liking for jazz
a smack is a faint flavour, as in a smack of garlic

explanation.surface: A fondness for heroin, or for a slap.
explanation.definitionFit: A preference or fondness is a taste for something, and a flavour is also a taste.

clue.text: Naval officer captures British force? Excellent!

indicators.note: the officer takes the British letter prisoner, holding it inside

parts.note: an admiral is a senior naval officer
E is the physics symbol for electromotive force; the question mark admits the stretch

explanation.surface: A navy man seizes a British unit, and someone applauds.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the symbol for electromotive force, hence the question mark on 'force'.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirable and excellent both express high praise; the exclamation suits the clue's applause.

clue.text: Atmosphere on beach's good? People initially show affectation!

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: an air is an atmosphere or feel
sand is the beach; the possessive adds no letter
G is good
a race is a people

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of show

explanation.surface: Seaside atmosphere is pleasant, with people putting on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on airs and graces is affected, pretentious behaviour.

clue.text: Founder of fell race could be leading

indicators.note: the rearranged letters lead, coming before the hill
says the letters of race could be something else, a rearrangement

parts.note: a fell is a northern English hill; a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: Whoever started a fell race could be the one out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: A fell race is a British hill-running event; here 'fell' just means hill, giving TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who founds or originates something is its maker or originator.

clue.text: A spouse's posh recipe for ham

parts.note: a mate is a husband or wife, the possessive adding no letter
U means upper-class, posh
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A wife's upmarket way of cooking gammon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' is not meat but an unskilled performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is an unskilled performer or radio enthusiast, a non-professional.

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words a sweatshirt

explanation.surface: Tuck yourself into a sweatshirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is British schoolchildren's slang for food and snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal nouns for food, the sort a pupil buys at the tuck shop.

parts.note: an artisan is a skilled craftsman

explanation.surface: A woman called Penny hires a craftsman to work below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A resistance fighter in occupied territory belongs to the underground movement.

clue.text: Clan to run off at night

indicators.note: off says the letters of Clan to run go wrong, out of order

explanation.surface: A Scottish clan flees under cover of darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal describes things active or happening by night, like owls.

clue.text: Supporter for a girl in depression

indicators.note: the girl's pronoun goes inside the depression

parts.note: a dent is a hollow, a depression
her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: A supporter for a girl who is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests mood, but it is a hollow, a dent.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or devotee of a cause, a backer.

clue.text: Engineers popped off and put right

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps
popped off is slang for died

explanation.surface: Engineers made a sudden exit and then set things right.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedied and put right are both past-tense verbs for correcting or fixing something.

indicators.note: the man takes the compass letter inside him

parts.note: mister is a form of address for a man
N, north, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A man accepts guidance in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A minster is a large or important church, as with York Minster.

indicators.note: the sad letters surround, catching, the cold letter

parts.note: unhappy means sad
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A miserable swimmer who has come down with a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: The scad is a fish, also called horse mackerel; fish are crossword swimmers.

indicators.note: the opening letter goes inside the footwear

parts.note: boots are footwear

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of sales

explanation.surface: A rise in sales, at first in shoes and boots.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost is to raise or increase; both are verbs in the present tense.

clue.text: Construction worker to start going topless

indicators.note: the word for starting loses its first letter, its top in a down answer

parts.note: to trigger is to set off, start

explanation.surface: A builder decides to start working shirtless.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigger erects scaffolding or rigging on building sites.

clue.text: Top lost from conditioner more frequently

indicators.note: the first letter is removed from the word for conditioner

parts.note: fabric conditioner is a softener

explanation.surface: A bottle of conditioner has lost its cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative adverbs: oftener is an older form meaning with greater frequency.

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T
an heir is a beneficiary of a will

explanation.surface: Someone's ideal beneficiary in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A gender-neutral possessive pronoun used for a single person of unspecified sex.

clue.text: In song, tease a champion of popular rights

indicators.note: the teasing word is placed inside the song

parts.note: a tune is a song
to rib is to tease

explanation.surface: A protest song that mocks its target in the name of the people.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman tribunes were officials defending plebeians; the word now means a people's defender.

indicators.note: out signals the letters of Cecil spat are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Cecil spits out a remark expressing disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spat' reads as part of the speech verb but is anagram fodder; 'out' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling doubt about a claim is being sceptical, a straightforward synonym.

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier in crosswords

explanation.surface: A soldier picked up some information at school.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British informal slang for information or the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: A school of art or writing is a style or category, which is what a genre is.

clue.text: Advertising is, in certain environment, an eye-opener

indicators.note: the certain word forms the surroundings for the other letters

parts.note: certain means sure
PR is public relations, publicity

explanation.surface: Advertising, in a world of certainty, proves revealing.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is something startling or unexpected, which is a revelation.

parts.note: an arm is a branch or power of authority, as in the arm of the law
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Those in power permitted some decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A band or bracelet worn around the upper arm is an ornament, a piece of jewellery.
